title: orders-api p95 climbed and clients saw timeouts
symptoms: pool wait count climbing on the affected service
brief increase in held database connections while waiting on I/O
increase in 5xx responses seen by callers
database wait events coinciding with the latency climb
p95 and p99 latency climbing together
observed_signals: latency jumped by more than 10x while CPU stayed only moderately higher
timeout-related WARN/ERROR rate on the service rose from near zero
db_connection_utilization on the service rose from a mid-20s baseline toward saturation
downstream_latency_ms on callers increased as they waited on orders-api

timeline.event: request duration histograms shifted right on orders-api
connection wait logs appeared on orders-api
error rate returned toward baseline after the change

contributing_factors: a recent deploy introduced a path that did not close connections
concurrency was higher than the pool was sized for
resolution: rolled back the release that stopped returning connections to the pool
enabled pool leak detection and added a saturation alert at 80%
confirmed wait queue dropped after the rollback
lessons_learned: do not raise pool size without checking for leaks
alert on pool utilization and acquire timeouts, not only on 5xx
